full_judgment:
Upon an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act, a Rule was issued calling upon the respondent to show cause as to why the delay of 1930 days in preferring the appeal should not be condoned or such other or further order or orders passed as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

 6. Mr. Nurul Islam, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, submits that as the petitioner was ill for a long period being attacked with paralysis from 7-2-88 to 1-3-96 and as he was residing at his village home at that time and as the trial took place at Rajshahi in his absence, he was not aware of the criminal proceeding against him and the order of conviction passed against him. He further submits that the petitioner, who is a practicing Advocate of the Dinajpur District Bar, for the first time came to know about the judgment and order of conviction against him on 27-5-96 when he was arrested by the local police and thereafter on obtaining certified copy of necessary papers he preferred the present appeal with an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act to condone the delay in filing the appeal. 

 10. Accordingly, the petition under section 5 of the Limitation Act is allowed and the delay in filing the appeal is condoned.
